title: Qualification forms and automated triage rules for hosted multi-output requests
creator: Marcus Lee
description:
Problem statement: Enterprise teams submit a high volume of hosted API feature requests that combine chat, streaming, function/tool calls, and structured outputs. Manual triage is slow, inconsistent across SRE/PM/Legal, and creates onboarding friction for high-value tenants. Goal: Design a lightweight qualification form + a ruleset engine that automatically classifies incoming requests into priority lanes (SLA-tiered), required review paths (security/compliance/product), and suggested runtime configs (model family, streaming vs poll, batching hints).

Scope and deliverables:
1) Intake form fields and validation (tenant metadata, use-case, expected qps, data sensitivity, regulatory region, success metrics, example prompts/payloads, expected structured schema).
2) Machine-readable triage rule set expressed as prioritized predicates (e.g., if tenant_sla == enterprise AND data_sensitivity == PII -> route to Legal+Dedicated).
3) Default mapping from triage outcome to onboarding artifacts: suggested model variants, release channel (canary/gradual), required guardrails (response logging, redact), and rollout ETA buckets.
4) Implementation plan: lightweight serverless rule-evaluator (prototype), integration points with Support/CS intake form, and console flags for manual override.

Success metrics:
- Reduce median triage time from 48h -> 8h for enterprise requests.
- Increase first-pass completeness of intake forms to >85%.
- Correctly auto-classify 90% of enterprise requests into the right review path during pilot.

Acceptance criteria:
- Canonical intake form defined + JSON schema stored in Confluence.
- Prototype rule table (10 rules) implemented and demoable against historical 60 requests.
- PM/Legal/SRE sign-off on rule semantics and audit logs.

Non-goals:
- Full automation of approvals (we still require human sign-off for high-risk routes).
- Replacement of tenant-specific concierge onboarding for top-tier customers.
comments: 2026-01-13 Marcus Lee: Kickoff notes + sample set of 63 recent enterprise intake emails uploaded. Observed common missing fields: expected qps, schema sample, and data residency. Proposed minimum required fields in the form.

2026-01-19 Elena Martinez: Workshop with Legal and SRE. Legal requires a single-question sensitivity classifier (none/low/medium/high) plus attachments for any PII examples. SRE pushed for an explicit peakTPS and latency SLO per request to recommend Dedicated vs Hosted routing.

2026-01-22 Engineering feedback (Alexei Novak): Prototype rule-evaluator implemented as a step function + small rules table. Trade-off: rule expressivity vs explainability. Chose a simple predicate language (field operator value) that can be logged and audited.

2026-01-27 PM review (Hannah Cho): Added 'tenant revenue signal' as a soft priority flag; we will not hard-route on revenue without CS approval. Also flagged need for a manual override in Console for misclassifications.

2026-02-01 Elena Martinez: Ran pilot against 60 archived requests. Results: 82% auto-classified correctly, 10% inconclusive (missing fields), 8% misclassified (edge cases with unusual tool-chains). Action: add two rules to handle nested function calls and require schema attachments for structured-output requests.

2026-02-03 Legal (Priya Raman): Signed off on sensitivity classifier wording but requested 'audit path' for any auto-approval that skips manual Legal review. Added requirement to persist the rule decision and responsible approver in audit logs.

2026-02-04 Marcus Lee: Updated the intake JSON schema and created follow-up tickets: ENG-12764 (rule-evaluator infra hardening), PM-953422 (pilot rollout plan), DES-3142 (form UX polish). Preparing RFC for the executive review on 2026-02-10.
decision_log: Initial rule language: predicate triples (field operator value) evaluated top-to-bottom. For ambiguous cases, mark 'inconclusive' and flag for concierge review. Chosen runway: pilot with 10 rules targeting top-5 complaint categories: missing SLA, PII, multi-tool chains, structured outputs without schema, and high-throughput tenants.
next_steps: 1) Finalize JSON schema and host in Confluence (owner: Marcus). 2) Engineering to harden the prototype and add audit logging (owner: Alexei, ENG-12764). 3) Run 2-week pilot with CS on inbound enterprise requests; measure triage accuracy and time savings. 4) Iterate on rules and roll out console override.
notes_for_reviewers: Please focus review on: (a) whether the sensitivity classifier covers legal needs, (b) whether the rule outputs are actionable for runtime routing (model/dedicated/rollback), and (c) logging requirements for audit trail. If you disagree with a rule, comment with a suggested replacement predicate and rationale.
